preservedMechanisms.obligation: Earliest passive lifecycle setup and actual Page ownership
preservedMechanisms.observation: Present registers the passive script on the parent BrowserContext before the native popup action, retains the popup from the early popup event, attaches the active-page error listener and stages creation before later readiness/document operations. Share registers the context init script before creating its page and attaches active ownership before goto. File registers the supplied passive script before context.newPage and transfers the complete handle to the callback before file navigation. Its callback first assigns stashedHandle, so later metadata/staging/navigation failures still leave the finally block with the actual context to close.
preservedMechanisms.boundary: This proves static registration/ownership ordering, not execution timing or external Playwright/Reveal dispatcher equivalence.

preservedMechanisms.obligation: Raw document identity and exact root manifest/cardinality
preservedMechanisms.observation: Manifests require a nonempty array, exact three-key entries, nonempty string fields and uniqueness checking. Observed roots require equal cardinality and one-use exact slideId/elementId/gameType tuple matches. Present/share/file stage actual URL/documentId/timeOrigin before binding. Identity validation rejects about:blank/missing discriminators, compares normalized planned URLs with hashes ignored and checks the bound documentId/timeOrigin/normalized URL on subsequent reads. Bound identity is copied and cannot be rebound.
preservedMechanisms.boundary: Tuple/document validation remains connected; it does not make the immutable acceptance caller compatible, nor establish complete browser-versus-Node failure chronology in the live-root consumer.

preservedMechanisms.obligation: Early portable handle transfer and failure-safe lifecycle-surface cleanup
preservedMechanisms.observation: freshPortable's callback branch deliberately leaves cleanup to the transferred owner. visitSurface stores the handle before any further callback work. After navigation, document binding, before-network enforcement or visit failure, its finally still performs after-network inspection, stages settled diagnostics, collects live evidence and closes the actual context. Each after-inspection/live/close failure is independently recorded rather than replacing the runner error. Present/share likewise collect live evidence before safeClose; safeClose records a close occurrence.

preservedMechanisms.obligation: Portable setup/navigation failures and no-sink ownership
preservedMechanisms.observation: Sink callbacks are optional. Setup failures close an allocated context; no-callback navigation/readiness failures also close it. A close failure is attached to the actual setup/navigation Error's secondaryFailures and is separately dispatched when a sink exists. Generic generated-surface and content-field consumers continue to use actual returned Page/context handles and close in finally. Frame inspection without a sink still throws the first retained actual frame Error. No alternate fake handle or successful fallback was added.
preservedMechanisms.boundary: The callback-transfer path and generic no-sink cleanup have specific pre-existing failure limits enumerated separately below; this is not an unconditional claim that every generic helper failure exposes all errors.

preservedMechanisms.observation: Each sequentially awaited frame rejection is dispatched immediately in its catch before inspection proceeds to the next frame. Page errors dispatch synchronously in their event callback. The ledger assigns occurrence order at recordError arrival. This preserves the original chronological-arrival meaning rather than substituting popup/success-key semantics.

preservedMechanisms.obligation: E06-03 — actual Node Error identity and separate sidecar
preservedMechanisms.observation: An actual frame Error is retained as rawError and forwarded unchanged; frameUrl is supplied as separate metadata. materializeEnvelope returns an actual Error unchanged. serializeError reads frameUrl from metadata without assigning it to the original Error. Without a sink, the thrown fallback is frameFailures[0].rawError. With a sink, the common-ledger primary can be an earlier independent occurrence.

preservedMechanisms.obligation: Strict portable success shape and cumulative before/after enforcement
preservedMechanisms.observation: Inspection refreshes actual handle diagnostics before a frame-error throw or empty-network assertions. Frame failures remain cumulative across inspections. Success requires empty socketAttempts, httpAttempts and errors and returns exactly {protocol,httpAttempts,socketAttempts,errors}. Pending lifecycle file journeys inspect before and after the visit while routes block HTTP(S)/WebSocket activity from context setup onward. The callback diagnostics field is the strict before-result, not a substituted raw object.

preservedMechanisms.obligation: E06-04 and E06-05 — local snapshot order and recursive provenance
preservedMechanisms.observation: The shared snapshot reader invokes state before UI; live-root dispatch lists actual stateError before uiError. Browser recursive envelopes carry phase/stack/cause/rootInstanceId/document/timeOrigin/URL and materialization/serialization retain those fields. Primary measured evidence propagates rootInstanceId/timeOrigin. These local credits do not excuse the separate live-root document-before-browser ordering defect.

collectLive independently catches diagnostics versus screenshot/PNG-attachment failures, so diagnostics failure does not skip the screenshot attempt. finalize records runner failure, missing baseline prerequisite, actual source GET/comparison failure and measured JSON-attachment failure. JSON attachment failure is recorded before produceThrow. Multi-error exposures refresh on later occurrences, preserving stable serialized identities and identity-based caller-ledger append behavior; a sole occurrence returns the actual Error without synthetic allErrors/errorLedger exposure. A failed GET is not represented as successful source equality.

preservedMechanisms.obligation: S10-C2 exposure seam, 09-S4/09-S5 and original E06-01 preservation
preservedMechanisms.observation: All three ingestion exposures reconcile an existing entry's phase only from an explicit nonempty wrapper phase; metadata enrichment alone calls reconciliation with no new phase authority. serializeError uses the recorded explicit occurrence phase ahead of intrinsic Error.phase. Reconciliation updates the same serialized object via Object.assign. Genuine caller errorLedger references are ingested in caller order before secondaryFailures and allErrors; serialized-only objects are not materialized as occurrences. These are personally read cross-component observations, not borrowed independent Evidence11 conclusions.
preservedMechanisms.boundary: The integration owner remains accountable for the complete obligations and non-surface seams.

componentDefects.trigger: evaluateLiveRootObservation returns already observed stateError/uiError and an actual document identity that fails the bound identity assertion, such as a replacement document still containing game roots.
componentDefects.mechanism: collectLiveRootStates stages the complete result, then records the later Node documentIdentity exception before iterating rootData.rootErrors. The ledger makes that document exception primary/order-first; rootFailure additionally selects docIdentityError before the normalized browser errors. Both browser siblings survive, but their chronology and governing primary are wrong.
componentDefects.actualPath: visitSurface finally -> evidence.collectLive -> collectLivePageDiagnostics -> collectLiveRootStates -> ledger.recordError. The actual browser producer calls __nsReadRootSnapshot before it returns rootErrors/documentIdentity; the subsequent Node assertion cannot precede those getter occurrences.
componentDefects.repairMechanism: Preserve raw staging and every independent failure, normalize the already observed browser occurrences before the later Node document validation occurrence, and select the earliest applicable normalized failure rather than a document-first category. No repair performed or additional correction authorized.
componentDefects.integrationRequirement: Reconcile this finding with the evidence-ledger/collection component and the historical preservation credits. The scope inventory records live-evidence.js as unchanged, so do not label it an introduced Correction11 regression.

retainedFailurePathLimits.observation: The generic no-sink launchPresentPopup does not return its popup until domcontentloaded succeeds. If that wait rejects after popup creation, visitGeneratedSurfaces/withPresent have not entered their finally and do not possess the popup to close it. The lifecycle visitSurface caller is different: its separate early popup event retains ownership and still reaches collection/close.
retainedFailurePathLimits.disposition: A source-backed pre-existing generic limitation, not a new11 finding and not a waiver or newly authorized repair. Do not turn the preserved lifecycle cleanup into a claim that generic Present has equivalent early-failure ownership.

retainedFailurePathLimits.observation: Generic no-sink finally blocks directly await close. If both inspection/visit/navigation and close reject, the close rejection replaces the earlier thrown failure rather than preserving both; launchPresentSlidePopup's catch has the same direct-close masking shape. Lifecycle visitSurface uses safeClose plus the common ledger and does not share this limitation.
retainedFailurePathLimits.disposition: Source-backed existing error-path boundary. No introduced11 regression claim, blanket cleanliness claim, or new mandatory correction scope is inferred.

retainedFailurePathLimits.observation: onPageCreated is awaited outside freshPortable's setup/navigation catch and cleanup intentionally belongs to the transferred owner. The actual lifecycle callback stashes the handle before operations that could reject, satisfying that ownership seam. The generic withPortable function, however, only enters its own finally after freshPortable returns. A caller-provided options.onPageCreated therefore must itself own early cleanup/retention; passing it through withPortable alone does not establish the lifecycle guarantee.
retainedFailurePathLimits.disposition: Explicit ownership contract boundary, not a demand to restore helper-owned cleanup after transfer or an invented defect in the actual lifecycle callback.

completeRecordedExcludedScopeCandidate.consumerVisibleMechanism: evaluateActionCandidates returns candidates from the public, replaceable window.__nsRecordedPackets (:146-147). storeHealth (:148) checks only the lifecycle store. In-place mutation of an original packet is detected, because that packet object is also the retained native-action detail. Replacing the array, or replacing an element with a forged object, leaves the retained and private stores untouched, so health stays true. extractActionBracket (observation.js:107-131) then builds the action bracket from the forged packet: rootEventsBefore/After, stateAfter and tCapture/tBubble, which witness.js:44-63 adopts as the Start baseline. This is the same public-store replacement model as N07-04, applied to the packet store.
completeRecordedExcludedScopeCandidate.title: Bind returned action packets to the integrity-checked native-action records
completeRecordedExcludedScopeCandidate.repairNeeded: Inside evaluateActionCandidates, derive candidates from, or verify each one against, the closure-retained native-action entries. For example, expose a private read of native-action details by sequence, or verify that each candidate is identical to the retained entry's detail and matches its private JSON clone. Report a recorder:store error when they diverge. evaluatePreActionCursor's lastSeq source (:36-37) needs the same binding.
completeRecordedExcludedScopeCandidate.scopeDecision: Original N07-04/N07-05 explicitly cover lifecycle store integrity. Extending identical checks to separately replaceable action-packet storage is not automatically a required cutover; no new repair scope authorized.
